question: kappa(theta) = least order of a tree carrying a nowhere-vanishing theta-eigenvector
why: BGM Lemma 4.2 forces every component of a theta-Aomoto subset to be such a tree, so kappa(theta)*cc(G[S]) <= |S| replaces the crude |S| >= 2 cc(G[S]) in the degree-spread chain, giving Delta > (delta-2) kappa(theta) + 2.
method: exhaustive over all trees on n vertices by Prufer sequence with dedup on (spectrum, degree sequence); an eigenvalue qualifies iff some vector in its eigenspace is nonzero at every vertex, tested as min over i of the norm of row i of an orthonormal eigenspace basis > 1e-7
range: all 522,958 free trees of order 2 through 19, generated by Beyer-Hedetniemi level sequences with AHU canonical forms at the centroid, tree counts self-tested against the known free-tree numbers
pattern: the running minimum drops only at even n = 2m and equals 2 cos(m pi/(2m+1)) = 2 sin(pi/(2(2m+1))), attained by the path P_{2m} at k = m, which qualifies because gcd(m, 2m+1) = 1

refuted_predictions.P83a: REFUTED for odd n. The minimum over trees of order exactly n is attained by a path only for even n; at n = 5, 7, 9 a non-path tree beats every path.
refuted_predictions.P83b: REFUTED in the same way. The gcd formula min over gcd(k,n+1)=1 of |2 cos(k pi/(n+1))| gives the correct value only for even n.

surviving_claim: the RUNNING minimum, over all trees of order at most n, is the path value at the largest even order, and is unaffected by the odd-order failures because odd orders never improve on the preceding even order
conjecture: kappa(theta) >= 2m whenever |theta| < 2 cos(m pi/(2m+1)); verified exhaustively for all trees of order at most 9, i.e. for m <= 4
asymptotic: 2 sin(pi/(2(2m+1))) ~ pi/(n+1), so kappa(theta) is about pi/|theta|
not_formalized: the path eigenvector formula (classical) and the conjecture (a conjecture)

matching_bound.statement: every nonzero eigenvalue of a forest satisfies theta^2 >= m_nu/m_(nu-1)
matching_bound.proof: mu_F = x^(n-2nu) Q(x^2); the nu roots of Q are the squares of the nonzero eigenvalues and are positive; Vieta on the bottom two coefficients gives sum of reciprocals = m_(nu-1)/m_nu; each positive term is at most the sum
matching_bound.max_ratio_formula_conjectured: binom(m+1,2) at order 2m (attained by the path), m^2/2 at order 2m+1
matching_bound.constant: gives kappa(theta) >~ 2 sqrt2/|theta| = 2.828/|theta| against the true pi/|theta| = 3.142/|theta|

godsil.theorem: Godsil, proving a conjecture of Gutman: among trees on 2m vertices WITH A PERFECT MATCHING the path minimizes the smallest positive eigenvalue, namely 2 cos(m pi/(2m+1))
godsil.why_it_does_not_close_the_question: a nowhere-vanishing eigenvector does not force a perfect matching
godsil.conclusion: those trees are outside Godsil's hypothesis but are well above the path values 0.4450 and 0.3473, so they do not affect the minimum

literature_error_caught: a web summary claimed Hong proved the path minimizes the smallest positive eigenvalue among ALL trees on n vertices. FALSE: the 5-vertex chair has char poly x^5-4x^3+2x, smallest positive eigenvalue 2 cos(3 pi/8) = 0.7654, below P_5's value of 1.
superseded_earlier_range: the earlier order<=9 run used Prufer enumeration deduped on (spectrum, degree sequence), which MERGES cospectral trees: it found 45 trees of order 9 where there are 47. The two lost trees do not change the minimum, but every order-9 figure from that run was computed over an incomplete set.

C1_exact.claim: max of m_(nu-1)/m_nu over trees of order 2m is binom(m+1,2), attained by the path; over order 2m+1 it is m^2/2
C1_exact.verified: exactly, in integer arithmetic, for every order up to 19

C2_spectral.claim: running minimum of |theta| over nowhere-vanishing eigenpairs of trees of order at most n equals 2 cos(m pi/(2m+1)) for the largest even 2m <= n

P84.c: HOLDS, the running minimum at order 9 is unchanged by the two recovered trees

C1_resolved.split: trees of order 2m with a perfect matching, versus without
C1_resolved.with_perfect_matching: PROVED. A tree has at most one perfect matching, so m_nu = 1 and the ratio is m_(m-1). Gutman's classical theorem, that the path is the unique maximiser of m_k for each fixed k among trees on n vertices, gives m_(m-1) <= binom(m+1,2) with equality only for the path. Verified separately here: over all trees of order at most 16, zero violations of m_k(T) <= m_k(P_n) for any k.
C1_resolved.without_perfect_matching: OPEN, but exhausted to order 20. The maximum is (m-1)(3m-4)/6, one third of the (m-1)-st pentagonal number, falling short of binom(m+1,2) by exactly (5m-2)/3.
C1_resolved.what_is_still_needed: only the inequality, not the exact value: any argument that a tree of even order without a perfect matching has ratio below binom(m+1,2)
